newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan troops halt advance following rebel raid,
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan troops halt advance following rebel raid,

text.p: Troops on a month-long thrust into Tamil Tiger rebel areas in Sri Lanka's north temporarily halted their advance to patch up defences breached in a rebel assault this week, military officials and a newspaper said on Friday.
"Our troops are consolidating their positions," a Defence Ministry spokesman said.
The independent Island newspaper said troops had halted near Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital, Colombo.
It quoted unnamed security forces officials as saying ground commanders were assessing the situation while fresh troops had been brought in to close the breach.
The Defence Ministry, however, said the operation was continuing.
More than 1,000 rebels attacked the military's defences at Thandikulam and Nochchimoddai, near Vavuniya, on Tuesday, the Defence Ministry has said.

But security forces held on and by Wednesday had driven the rebels back, it said. Analysts and diplomats have said the daring Tamil rebel counterattack, while costly for both sides, would not halt the military's offensive against the rebels.

Military officials said the army's death toll in the raid was expected to be around 140 but the LTTE, which seek a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, have said more than 300 soldiers were killed along with 50 guerrillas.
The Defence Ministry said rebel radio indicated that 300 LTTE fighters had died in the assault. Earlier ministry estimates said 210 rebels died.
Some 20,000 troops began the current offensive into rebel areas, dubbed "Operation Jaya Sikuru" (Sure of Victory), on May 13.

The push through the brush jungles of the northern Wanni region is intended to open a highway between Vavuniya and the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north. The troops have captured key rebel towns in the area.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as international media have not been allowed into the war zone.

In a fresh attack in the east on Friday morning, rebels stopped a passenger bus and shot dead three policemen and two civilians at Onthachchimadam, near Kallar, in Batticaloa district 240 km (150 miles) east of Colombo.
The policemen were going home on leave.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is much higher.
